description: Count the unique cover arcs in the transitive reduction of a bounded simple DAG.

source.title: The Transitive Reduction of a Directed Graph
source.authors: A. V. Aho, M. R. Garey, and J. D. Ullman
source.primary_reference: SIAM Journal on Computing 1(2), 131-137 (1972), DOI 10.1137/0201008; the DAG reduction is unique and removes exactly arcs with alternate paths.
source.copyright: The cited publication is used as an algorithmic reference only; the package is independently authored.

input.graph: Simple directed acyclic graph. Vertex IDs are arbitrary; each ordered arc occurs once, and loops, repeated arcs, and directed cycles are invalid.

output.meaning: Number of arcs in the unique transitive reduction.

algorithm_details.primary: Compute non-reflexive Boolean transitive closure. For each direct arc u->v, mark it redundant if a distinct intermediate vertex w has direct edge u->w and a positive-length path w->v; otherwise retain it. Cycles are rejected by a reachable diagonal bit.
algorithm_details.independent_oracle: Validate acyclicity with Kahn's algorithm, then remove each original arc in turn and run BFS from its tail. The arc is redundant exactly when its head remains reachable without it.
algorithm_details.tie_rules: Vertex and intermediate scans use ascending IDs; input edge order is retained for deletion checks. The scalar count is independent of output ordering.
algorithm_details.arithmetic_bound: A simple DAG on at most eight vertices has at most 28 arcs. The output and all graph counts fit signed 64-bit arithmetic; the closure uses at most eight bits per row.
